dag.title: DAG settings
dag.selectHint: Select a node on the canvas to edit it.

general.yamlNote: Generates an Airflow 3.4 YAML DAG. Task groups and Python tasks aren't supported in YAML.
general.yamlUnsupportedNodes: This DAG contains task groups or Python tasks — switch to Python output or remove them.
general.ownerLinksHelp: Owner name → link (https:// or mailto:) shown in the Airflow UI.
general.failFastHelp: Stop all running tasks as soon as one task fails.
general.nativeTemplates: Render templates as native Python objects
general.nativeTemplatesHelp: Jinja results keep their type (list, dict, int) instead of becoming strings.
general.rerunLatestHelp: Cleared tasks run against the newest DAG version instead of the version of the original run.
general.dagIdHelp: Unique id of the DAG in Airflow; also the file name. Letters, digits, '_', '-', '.'.
general.displayNameHelp: Name shown in the Airflow UI instead of the DAG id (optional).
general.descriptionHelp: Short description shown in the Airflow DAG list.
general.tagsHelp: Labels for filtering DAGs in the Airflow UI and for access policies.
general.outputModeHelp: Generated Python: a readable DAG file. Loader: the spec is stored as JSON and built at parse time.
general.teamHelp: Multi-team Airflow (3.2+): the team owning this DAG; pickers then show its connections, pools and variables.
general.maxActiveRunsHelp: Maximum number of runs of this DAG running at the same time (default: [core] max_active_runs_per_dag).
general.maxActiveTasksHelp: Maximum number of task instances of this DAG running at once, across all runs.
general.runTimeoutHelp: A run still going after this many seconds is marked failed (dagrun_timeout).
general.maxConsecutiveFailedHelp: Pause the DAG automatically after this many failed runs in a row (0 = never).
general.pausedUponCreationHelp: New DAGs start paused: nothing runs until someone unpauses it in Airflow.
general.sourcePolicyHelp: How the Python DAG file is written on deploy: generated from the spec, or the existing hand-written file patched with each change (comments, formatting and ordering kept).

sourcePolicyNote.generate: Each deploy writes the file AutoAir generates. A file changed outside AutoAir is never overwritten silently.
sourcePolicyNote.preserve: Each deploy patches only what changed into the existing file; a change it cannot apply stops the deploy with an explanation.
sourcePolicyNote.strict-preserve: Like preserve, but also refuses changes that would replace values written as variables, change an operator class or move a task between groups.

general.sourcePolicyNotApplicable: Applies to Python output only: loader and YAML files are always generated.

schedule.catchupHelp: Create runs for every missed interval between the start date and now.
schedule.timezoneHelp: Start/end dates are local to it and schedules without their own timezone (presets like @daily, cron, intervals) run in it — DST aware.
schedule.startDateHelp: First logical date the scheduler considers. Runs before it are never created.
schedule.endDateHelp: No runs are scheduled after this date (optional).

defaults.help: Applied to every task unless the task overrides them.
defaults.dependsOnPastHelp: A task runs only if its previous run succeeded.
defaults.ownerHelp: Owner shown in the Airflow UI for every task (default_args.owner).
defaults.retriesHelp: How many times a failed task is retried before it is marked failed.
defaults.executionTimeoutHelp: A task running longer than this many seconds is killed and failed.
defaults.poolHelp: Pool limiting how many of these tasks run at once (Admin → Pools). Empty: default_pool.
defaults.queueHelp: Executor queue the tasks are sent to (Celery/Kubernetes worker queues). Empty: the default queue.
defaults.emailHelp: Addresses notified on failure/retry when e-mail alerts are enabled (needs SMTP configured).
defaults.emailOnFailureHelp: Send an e-mail to the addresses above when a task fails.

deadlines.title: Deadline alerts
deadlines.help: Notify when a DAG run hasn't finished by a deadline computed from a reference time.
deadlines.unsupported: The target Airflow version does not support deadline alerts.
deadlines.name: Name

referenceHelp.dagrun_queued_at: Counted from when the run was queued.
referenceHelp.dagrun_logical_date: Counted from the run's logical date.
referenceHelp.fixed_datetime: Counted from a fixed point in time.
referenceHelp.average_runtime: Counted from the average duration of recent runs.

deadlines.averageMaxRunsHelp: Number of recent runs used to compute the average.
deadlines.synchronousHelp: Execute the notifier in the scheduler instead of the triggerer.
deadlines.nameHelp: Name of this deadline alert (shown in Airflow).
deadlines.fixedDatetimeHelp: The run must finish before this moment, otherwise the callback fires.

env.help: Overrides applied when previewing or deploying to an environment (dev / staging / prod…).
env.unknownHelp: Not configured on the AutoAir server.
env.paramsDefaultsHelp: Replace the default of declared params in this environment. Leave empty to inherit.
env.selectorHelp: Validation, the deploy preview and deploys apply this environment's overlay. The Code tab and code mode show the base DAG (code mode edits it).
env.overrideScheduleHelp: Use a different schedule in this environment.
env.pausedHelp: Paused state of the DAG when it is created in this environment.
env.overrideTagsHelp: Replace the DAG tags in this environment.
env.tagsHelp: Tags used in this environment instead of the DAG's.
env.addLabelHelp: Name of an environment (dev, staging, prod…) whose overrides you want to edit.

mapping.title: Connection & Variable mapping
mapping.help: Ids used in the DAG (logical) and the ids this environment's Airflow has. Applied to *_conn_id parameters, {{ conn.<id> }} / {{ var.value.<key> }} templates and literal Variable.get / get_connection calls when previewing or deploying as this environment.
mapping.uncheckedHelp: Airflow could not be asked (unreachable or no permission to list connections/variables).
mapping.secretsHint: Ids missing from the metastore can still come from a secrets backend or environment variables; deploys are not blocked.

connections.title: Connections
connections.missing: Connection '{{id}}' is not in Airflow's metastore.

variables.title: Variables
variables.missing: Variable '{{id}}' is not in Airflow's metastore.

mapping.invalid: Use letters, digits, '.', '_' or '-'. Not saved until valid.

docs.label: Documentation (markdown)
docs.help: Shown on the DAG page in Airflow.

params.help: Run parameters (airflow.sdk.Param) — validated with JSON Schema, shown in the trigger form and available in templates as params.<name>.
params.duplicateName: A param with this name already exists.
params.name: Name
params.typesHelp: Select several to allow a union; include null to make the param optional.
params.defaultMismatch: The default does not match the declared type(s).
params.noDefaultRequired: No default: the value must be provided when triggering.
params.title: Title
params.descriptionMdHelp: Rendered as markdown in the trigger form; takes precedence over the description.
params.enumHelp: Renders a drop-down in the trigger form.
params.valuesDisplayHelp: Labels shown instead of the raw enum values.
params.itemsHelp: JSON Schema of the list items, e.g. {"type": "string"}.
params.examplesHelp: JSON list of suggestions shown in the trigger form.
params.constHelp: JSON value the param must always equal (read-only in the form).

preview.title: Trigger form preview
preview.help: How Airflow's “Trigger DAG” form will look, with live validation.

params.titleHelp: Label shown in the trigger form instead of the param name.
params.sectionHelp: Groups params into collapsible sections of the trigger form.
params.descriptionHelp: Help text shown under the field in the trigger form.
params.formatHelp: Input format the trigger form uses (date, e-mail, multi-line text…).
params.patternHelp: Regular expression the value must match.

raw.title: Raw code DAG
raw.help: Schedule, default arguments, tasks and everything else are defined in the code. These settings only name, list and route the DAG in AutoAir.
raw.dagIdHelp: Must be the dag_id the code defines; it also names the stored files.
raw.descriptionHelp: Shown in AutoAir's DAG list (the code's own description is what Airflow shows).
raw.tagsHelp: Labels for AutoAir's DAG list and search (the code's tags are what Airflow shows).
raw.environments: Environment overlays and connection/variable mapping do not apply to raw code: the same file is deployed to every environment.
raw.displayNameHelp: Shown in AutoAir's DAG list (the code's own display_name is what Airflow shows).

menu.dsAdd: add days to a date string

preview.label: Preview
preview.logicalDateAria: Sample logical date for template previews (UTC)
preview.unknownTitle: Only known when the task runs

jinja.assetScheduleWarning: Uses {{vars}}, but this DAG is scheduled on assets: asset-triggered runs have no logical date in Airflow 3, so these variables are undefined there (the task fails to render the template) and dag_run.logical_date is None. Prefer triggering_asset_events or run_id.

typeHelp.cron: CronTriggerTimetable: one run at each cron tick.
typeHelp.interval: DeltaTriggerTimetable: one run every fixed time delta.
typeHelp.multi_cron: MultipleCronTriggerTimetable: a run at every tick of any expression.
typeHelp.events: EventsTimetable: runs at the listed dates only.
typeHelp.assets: Runs when the asset condition is satisfied (asset events). No time based logical date.
typeHelp.assets_or_time: AssetOrTimeSchedule: runs on the time schedule and also when assets are updated.
typeHelp.assets_and_time: AssetAndTimeSchedule: the scheduled run happens only once the assets were updated.
typeHelp.partitioned_cron: CronPartitionTimetable: produces partitioned runs with a partition key.

schedule.noneHelp: The DAG only runs when triggered manually or via the API.
schedule.timezoneHelp: IANA timezone the expression is evaluated in (DST aware).
schedule.dataIntervalOn: Airflow 2 style: the run for an interval starts at its end; logical date = interval start.
schedule.dataIntervalOff: Trigger semantics (Airflow 3 default): the run starts at the scheduled time; logical date = run time.
schedule.intervalSecondsHelp: Optional: data_interval_start = run time minus this many seconds.
schedule.runImmediatelyHelp: When unpaused, run the latest missed tick right away instead of waiting for the next one.
schedule.restrictToEventsHelp: Manual runs also use the last event as their data interval.
schedule.batchAssetEventsHelp: Combine queued asset events into one run (default: one run per event).
schedule.assetsOrTimeHelp: Runs on the time schedule, and additionally whenever the asset condition is met.
schedule.assetsAndTimeHelp: A scheduled run is created only when the assets were updated since the previous run.
schedule.keyFormatHelp: strftime format of the partition key (empty: backend default).
schedule.mapperHelp: Maps upstream partition keys onto this DAG's partitions.

next.title: Next runs
next.manual: No automatic runs: the DAG is triggered manually.
next.assetDriven: Runs are driven by asset events, so there are no predictable run times.

alias.yearly: Once a year at midnight on January 1st
alias.annually: Once a year at midnight on January 1st
alias.monthly: At midnight on the first day of every month
alias.hourly: At the start of every hour

cron.domOrDow: on day {{days}} of the month or on {{weekdays}}
cron.presetHelp: Start from a common schedule, then fine-tune the fields.

schedule.timezoneInvalid: Unknown timezone: pick an IANA name such as Europe/Istanbul.
schedule.eventNHelp: A moment at which the DAG runs once.
schedule.eventsDescriptionHelp: Shown in the Airflow UI instead of the list of dates.
schedule.presetHelp: Airflow shortcut: @daily = midnight every day, @hourly = every hour…

assets.name: Asset name
assets.nameOrUri: Set a name or a URI.
assets.watchersHelp: Watchers listen to a message queue (MessageQueueTrigger) and emit asset events.
assets.schemeUnavailable: This scheme needs the {{provider}} provider package installed.

expr.title: Asset condition
expr.aliasHelp: AssetAlias: resolved at runtime to the assets a task attached to it.

assets.watcherNameHelp: Name of the watcher (unique within the asset).
assets.schemeHelp: URI scheme of the asset (s3, gs, file, postgres…).
assets.uriHelp: Identifies the data, e.g. s3://bucket/key. Producers and consumers must use the same URI.
assets.groupHelp: Group of the asset in the Airflow UI (default: asset).
assets.extraHelp: Free-form JSON metadata attached to the asset.
assets.eventExtraHelp: Stored as the event's extra; downstream DAGs read it via triggering_asset_events.
assets.sendEventHelp: Creates an asset event in Airflow (POST /api/v2/assets/events): DAGs scheduled on this asset may start.
assets.materializeHelp: Trigger the DAG that produces this asset.
assets.denied: You don't have permission for this (run:trigger). Ask an AutoAir admin.

node.label: Label (canvas only)
node.labelHelp: Shown on the canvas only; the task id stays what Airflow sees.
node.taskGroupHelp: TaskGroup this task belongs to; its id is prefixed with the group id in Airflow.

params.none: This operator has no configurable parameters.
params.templatedHelp: Rendered with Jinja at runtime (template field).
params.deferrableHelp: Frees the worker slot while waiting: the task suspends itself and a trigger resumes it. Requires a running triggerer.
params.deferrableTemplated: deferrable is set to “{{value}}”; the switch shows the literal state only.
params.sensorHelp: How the sensor waits: “poke” keeps a worker slot, “reschedule” releases it between checks.
params.notTemplated: This parameter is not a template field: Airflow passes the text verbatim without rendering it.

python.label: Python reference for {{name}}
python.invalid: Use an import path: package.module.name (letters, digits, _ and dots).
python.disabled: Python references are disabled on this server (allow_python_code).
python.help: An importable object (function, class, constant) the DAG imports and passes as this parameter.
python.helpRequired: This parameter takes a Python object (e.g. a function): give its import path. It must be importable where Airflow runs (provider package, plugins/ or dags/ folder).

function.label: Python function for {{name}}
function.help: Emitted in the DAG file and passed as this parameter. Imports at the top are allowed.

file.name: File name for {{name}}
file.runWithHelp: Optional interpreter, e.g. bash: the value becomes "bash <path>".
file.badName: Use a plain file name (letters, digits, . _ -).
file.help: Embedded in the DAG file and written to a file on every worker when the DAG is parsed; the parameter receives its path.
file.helpRun: Embedded in the DAG file and written to a file on every worker; the parameter receives "{{run}} <path>".

params.invalidJson: Not valid JSON: use ["a", "b"] for a list or {"key": "value"} for a mapping.
params.noDefault: No default available for {{names}}: enter a value.

args.connectUpstream: Connect an upstream task to use its output (XCom).

xcom.missingSource: The referenced task no longer exists

missing.connection: “{{id}}” is not in Airflow's metastore. Fine if it comes from a secrets backend or an AIRFLOW_CONN_* variable.
missing.pool: Pool “{{id}}” does not exist in Airflow yet; tasks wait until it is created.

inputs.title: Inputs from upstream tasks
inputs.help: Drag an output onto a parameter, or focus a parameter and press Insert.
inputs.empty: No upstream tasks. Connect tasks on the canvas to use their outputs (XCom).
inputs.noRunValues: No XCom values for this task in the selected run.

execution.displayNameHelp: Shown in the Airflow UI instead of the task id.
execution.dependsOnPastHelp: Run only if this task succeeded in the previous DAG run.
execution.maxActiveTisHelp: Limits concurrently running mapped instances of this task in a DAG run.
execution.backoffHelp: Multiplier for the retry delay on each attempt (0 = off).
execution.executorHelp: Run this task on a specific executor (multiple executors configured).
execution.executorConfigHelp: Executor specific settings, e.g. {"pod_override": …} for Kubernetes.
execution.ownerHelp: Owner shown for this task in the Airflow UI (overrides the DAG default).
execution.retriesCountHelp: How many times this task is retried before it is marked failed.
execution.retryDelayHelp: Seconds to wait before each retry.
execution.timeoutHelp: Kill and fail the task if it runs longer than this many seconds (execution_timeout).
execution.poolHelp: Pool limiting concurrency (Admin → Pools): the task waits for a free slot. Empty: default_pool.
execution.poolSlotsHelp: How many slots of the pool this task occupies while running (heavy tasks take more).
execution.queueHelp: Executor queue (Celery queue / Kubernetes worker group) that runs this task. Empty: the default queue.
execution.priorityWeightHelp: Higher values are scheduled first when slots are scarce.
execution.weightRuleHelp: How the effective priority is computed: downstream (sum of downstream), upstream, or absolute.

triggerRules.all_success: Runs when all upstream tasks succeeded.
triggerRules.all_failed: Runs when all upstream tasks failed or were upstream_failed.
triggerRules.all_done: Runs when all upstream tasks finished, whatever their state.
triggerRules.all_done_min_one_success: Runs when all upstream tasks finished and at least one succeeded.
triggerRules.all_done_setup_success: Runs when all upstream tasks finished and all upstream setup tasks succeeded (teardowns).
triggerRules.all_skipped: Runs when all upstream tasks were skipped.
triggerRules.one_success: Runs as soon as one upstream task succeeded.
triggerRules.one_done: Runs as soon as one upstream task succeeded or failed.
triggerRules.one_failed: Runs as soon as one upstream task failed.
triggerRules.none_failed: Runs when no upstream task failed (succeeded or skipped).
triggerRules.none_failed_min_one_success: Runs when no upstream task failed and at least one succeeded.
triggerRules.none_skipped: Runs when no upstream task was skipped.

behaviour.disabledHelp: Kept on the canvas but excluded from the generated DAG.
behaviour.setupTeardownHelp: Setup tasks create resources and teardown tasks clean them up; a teardown runs even when work tasks fail and does not fail the DAG run by itself.
behaviour.isSetupHelp: Clearing a work task also clears its setup.
behaviour.isTeardownHelp: Connect it downstream of its setup task; runs after the work in between.
behaviour.teardownTriggerRule: Teardown tasks normally use the all_done_setup_success trigger rule; a custom rule changes when cleanup runs.
behaviour.lineageHelp: Selective lineage (needs apache-airflow-providers-openlineage; useful with [openlineage] selective_enable).

callbacks.help: Notifiers are called when the event happens (Slack, e-mail, …). Several can run per event, in order.

retryPolicy.title: Exception retry policy
retryPolicy.help: Decide per exception class whether a failure is retried, fails immediately, or follows the task's retries.
retryPolicy.unsupported: The target Airflow version ({{version}}) does not support retry policies.
retryPolicy.exceptionHelp: Exception class (dotted path, e.g. requests.exceptions.Timeout) this rule matches.
retryPolicy.actionHelp: What to do when the exception is raised: retry, fail immediately or skip.
retryPolicy.delayHelp: Seconds to wait before the retry triggered by this rule.
retryPolicy.reasonHelp: Message recorded in the task log when the rule applies.
retryPolicy.matchSubclassesHelp: Also match subclasses of the exception.
retryPolicy.defaultHelp: Action for exceptions no rule matches.

mapping.title: Dynamic task mapping
mapping.help: Create one task instance per element at runtime.
mapping.expandHelpOperator: Each argument takes a list or the output of an upstream task; Op.partial(...).expand(arg=…).
mapping.expandHelpPython: Each argument becomes a function parameter receiving one element.
mapping.expandKwargsHelp: A list of dicts (or an upstream output producing one); each dict is one set of arguments.
mapping.mapIndexTemplateHelp: Jinja rendered per mapped instance and shown in the UI instead of the index.

data.outletsHelp: Assets updated when this task succeeds; asset-scheduled DAGs react to them.
data.inletsHelp: Lineage information; inlet events are available as inlet_events.

docs.docMdHelp: Shown in the task instance details in Airflow.
docs.expand: Open the documentation in a large window

operator.requiredAirflow: Airflow version required by the provider
operator.unsupported: This operator cannot be fully configured in the builder.
operator.pythonRefs: {{params}}: give an importable Python object (package.module.name) — it is imported by the generated DAG.
operator.pythonRefsAlt: {{params}}: give an importable Python object (package.module.name). To write the function in the builder instead, use a {{decorator}} node.

hitl.title: Human-in-the-loop
hitl.help: The task pauses until someone answers in the Airflow UI.
hitl.subject: Subject
hitl.bodyHelp: Shown to the reviewer; Jinja is rendered.
hitl.multipleHelp: The reviewer may select several options.
hitl.defaultsHelp: Used when the request times out.
hitl.optionsMappingHelp: Which downstream task runs for each option; the others are skipped.
hitl.noDownstream: Connect downstream tasks to map options to them.
hitl.assignedUsersHelp: Only these users may respond (empty: anyone with access).
hitl.timeoutHint: The response timeout is the task's execution timeout (Execution tab).
hitl.subjectHelp: Title of the request shown to the person who has to respond (templated).
hitl.responseTimeoutHelp: Seconds to wait for a human response; afterwards the defaults are used (or the task fails).

decorators.task: Runs the function in the worker's Python environment.
decorators.branch: Return the task id(s) to follow; other downstream tasks are skipped.
decorators.short_circuit: Return a falsy value to skip all downstream tasks.
decorators.virtualenv: Runs in a fresh virtualenv with the given requirements.
decorators.external_python: Runs with an existing Python interpreter (pre-built venv).
decorators.sensor: Return True / PokeReturnValue when the condition is met; called repeatedly.
decorators.bash: Return a Bash command string; it is executed.
decorators.docker: Runs the function inside a Docker container.
decorators.kubernetes: Runs the function in a Kubernetes pod.
decorators.stub: Implemented by a language SDK task handler (Airflow ≥ 3.3, experimental).
decorators.branch_external_python: Branching with an existing Python interpreter (pre-built venv).
decorators.llm: common.ai: the function returns a prompt; an LLM answers it.
decorators.agent: common.ai: an agent with toolsets works on the returned instructions.
decorators.llm_branch: common.ai: an LLM picks the downstream task(s) to follow.
decorators.llm_sql: common.ai: an LLM writes and validates SQL for the returned question.

python.branchHint: Return one (or a list) of these downstream task ids:
python.branchNoDownstream: Connect downstream tasks to branch to.
python.bashHint: The returned string is run as a Bash command.
python.sensorHint: The function is called every poke interval until it returns True.
python.pythonPathHelp: Absolute path of the interpreter on the worker.
python.softFail: Skip instead of failing on timeout
python.ignoreDownstreamTriggerRulesHelp: Off: only direct downstream tasks are skipped and trigger rules apply further down.
python.otherKwargsHelp: Passed to the decorator as keyword arguments.
python.argumentsHelp: Become function parameters. Values can be literals, templates or upstream outputs (XCom).
python.extraParametersHelp: Parameters without a bound value (e.g. keys provided by expand_kwargs).
python.bodyHelp: Use `return` to push a value to XCom.
python.multipleOutputsHelp: Push each key of a returned dict as its own XCom.
python.noKeysDetected: No `return {…}` dict literal found; keys can still be referenced manually.
python.queueHelp: Queue routed to a language SDK coordinator (Java, Go, TypeScript). The function body is not used.
python.isResultHelp: Its return value becomes the DAG run's result (dagRuns/{id}/wait API).
python.usesLoopContextHelp: Adds a keyword-only `loop` parameter: loop.index, loop.previous, loop.result, loop.max_iterations.
python.functionNameHelp: Python function name; also the default task id. Must be a valid identifier.
python.pythonVersionHelp: Python version of the virtualenv (e.g. 3.12); empty = same as the worker.
python.systemSitePackagesHelp: Let the virtualenv see packages installed on the worker.
python.imageHelp: Container image the function runs in (must contain a compatible Python).
python.dockerUrlHelp: Docker daemon to use, e.g. unix://var/run/docker.sock or tcp://host:2375.
python.autoRemoveHelp: Remove the container when it finishes.
python.namespaceHelp: Kubernetes namespace the pod is created in.
python.podNameHelp: Name prefix of the pod (a random suffix is added).
python.inClusterHelp: Use the in-cluster service account instead of a kube config.
python.pokeIntervalHelp: Seconds between two checks of the condition.
python.sensorTimeoutHelp: Fail (or skip with soft fail) when the condition is still false after this many seconds.
python.modeHelp: poke keeps a worker slot while waiting; reschedule frees it between checks.
python.softFailHelp: Mark the task skipped instead of failed on timeout.
python.aiCodeHelp: Describe what the task should do and review the generated code as a diff, or ask for an explanation.

group.prefix: Prefix task ids with group id
group.help: Drag tasks into the group on the canvas. Edges to/from a group apply to all its tasks.
group.loopHelp: Repeat the group's tasks; the body must end in one task whose result feeds the condition and the next iteration (loop.previous).
group.untilHelp: Return True to stop. Leave empty for a fixed number of iterations. Not converging by the limit fails the gate.
group.tooltipHelp: Hover text of the group in the Airflow graph.
group.maxIterationsHelp: Upper bound on loop iterations (safety stop).
group.untilNameHelp: Task whose result decides when the loop stops.

edge.title: Dependency
edge.label: Label
edge.labelHelp: Rendered with airflow.sdk.Label, e.g. a branch condition.

icon.assignFailed: Could not set the default icon
icon.uploadHelp: Any PNG, JPEG, WebP, GIF or SVG. It is framed and resized here to a 64 px PNG (crisp at the 16–32 px used on the canvas).
icon.unreadable: This file is not an image the browser can read.
icon.name: Name

newConnection.title: New Airflow connection
newConnection.help: Created in Airflow with your permissions. Credentials are sent to Airflow and never stored by AutoAir.
newConnection.typeHelp: Connection type (hook) — decides which fields Airflow uses.
newConnection.rawExtraHelp: Keys here override the fields above.

template.lockedHelp: Fixed by the operator template: read-only here, and validation reports any change.

llm.title: LLM task
llm.promptHelp: Sent to the model; Jinja templates ({{ ds }}, {{ ti.xcom_pull(...) }}, {{ params.x }}) are rendered at run time.
llm.outputTypeHelp: Plain text, or a structured result: a pydantic model the answer must match (output_type).
llm.outputTypeOther: output_type holds a value this editor cannot show; edit it in the raw parameters.
llm.classNameHelp: Python class generated at module level of the DAG file.
llm.classNameInvalid: Use a Python class name starting with an upper-case letter (e.g. Sentiment).
llm.fieldChoicesHelp: Optional: the model must answer one of these (Literal).
llm.toolsetsHelp: Tools the agent may call. Each one uses an Airflow connection, resolved when the task runs.
llm.toolsetsOther_one: {{count}} toolset written as raw JSON is kept unchanged.
llm.toolsetsOther_other: {{count}} toolsets written as raw JSON are kept unchanged.
llm.allowedTablesHelp: Empty: every table the connection can read.
llm.allowWritesHelp: Lets the agent run INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE. Off: read-only queries.
llm.requireApprovalHelp: The task defers after generating its output until a reviewer approves or rejects it (HITL).
llm.approvalTimeoutHelp: Seconds to wait for the review; afterwards the task fails.
llm.allowModificationsHelp: The approved (possibly edited) output becomes the task result.
llm.hitlReviewHelp: A reviewer can approve, reject or request changes; the agent revises its answer.
llm.decoratorHint: The function returns the prompt; the model's answer is the task result.
llm.llmConnectionHelp: Connection of the model provider (pydantic-ai: OpenAI, Anthropic, Bedrock…).
llm.modelIdHelp: provider:model, e.g. openai:gpt-5 or anthropic:claude-sonnet-4-5 (empty: the connection's default).

blueprint.stepIdHelp: Task or group id the blueprint renders under (its step_id).
blueprint.versionHelp: Each version is its own template with its own config; switching keeps the values, check them against the new form.
blueprint.disabledHelp: Leave the step out of the generated DAG (kept on the canvas).
blueprint.runtime: The Airflow environment needs airflow-blueprint and the module {{module}} (the blueprint templates) to parse this DAG.
blueprint.missing: Blueprint {{name}} v{{version}} is not in the catalog: {{error}}
blueprint.noSchema: The config schema could not be read ({{error}}); the config is not checked.
blueprint.previewFailed: The preview could not be rendered: {{error}}
blueprint.previewHelp: The tasks this step renders with the current config appear here.
